answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. Consider a kernel as the anchor of the cost.
